title: Romania's 3.1-Mile Recycled Table Sets World Record
summary:
On September 12, 2026, about 20,000 people gathered in Bucharest, Romania, for a community meal at the "Uniting Table." Stretching 3.1 miles (4.99 kilometers), it set a new Guinness World Record for the longest table made from recycled materials.

The world record was just part of the goal. The event, organized by the nonprofit Bloom The World, also served as a fundraiser. It raised more than $110,000 for Romania's first psychiatric hospital for children, a hospital providing mental health care.

Currently, children in Bucharest who need mental health care are treated in an outdated facility. It has large, crowded wards that lack basic privacy. The new hospital is scheduled to open in 2027 and provide care for children with conditions such as depression, autism, and ADHD.

This was the second time Bloom achieved this record. In 2025, the nonprofit brought together 10,000 people around a 1.7-mile (2.7-kilometer) table made from recycled materials. That event was held in Alba Iulia, Romania. It focused on bringing people together and raising environmental awareness.

Bloom plans to recycle the materials from its latest record-breaking table again. This time, they will be used to make children's furniture.
why_it_matters: The event connects a community celebration with funding for children's mental health care and a plan to recycle materials into furniture.
